en: Oṃ. The Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, together with the commentary composed by the venerable Sāyaṇācārya;
now begins the ninth Maṇḍala.
In the ninth maṇḍala, there are [twenty-two] anuvākas.
In the first anuvāka, there are twenty-four sūktas.
Among these, the first sūkta, consisting of ten ṛks, begins with "svādiṣṭhayā."
Here it is enumerated: "With the most sweet [hymn], ten; Madhucchandas.
Madhucchandas, the son of Viśvāmitra, is the seer (ṛṣi).
According to the technical rules regarding the Prāvastaprīya hymns, the meter (chandas) is Gāyatrī.
According to the statement in the *Anuvākānukramaṇī*, "The ninth maṇḍala is the Pāvamāna, dedicated to Soma," the deity is Soma as characterized by the quality of *pavamāna* (the purifying one).
In the *Grāvastotra*, everything from the beginning of this [hymn] up to the penultimate verse of the half-hymn may optionally be omitted.

This is prescribed in the *Sūtra*: "The half-verse beginning with *prete vadantu*, and all that follows the penultimate verse [of the first half-hymn], as well as the entire second half-hymn beginning with *ā va ṛñje* and *pra vo grāvāṇaḥ*, may be inserted either between [the two halves], or after, or before."
"The *pāvamānī* verses are also [to be recited] according to their respective purposes until the drawing of the cups" (*Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra* 5.12).
Regarding the ritual of the *upāla*, the first [verse] is to be used when drawing the *maṇḍala* and so forth;
the *sūtra* has already been cited previously.

Flow forth, O Soma, with your sweetest and most intoxicating stream; you have been pressed for Indra to drink. 1. With your sweetest. Most intoxicating. Flow forth. O Soma. With your stream. For Indra. To drink. Pressed. 1.
O Soma, pressed out for Indra to drink, thou art poured forth to be drunk; flow, pour forth with a stream that is most sweet, most delicious, most intoxicating, and exceedingly gladdening.

The slayer of demons, the observer of all people, has prepared the womb; he has established his seat upon the firm foundation. 2. The slayer of demons, the observer of all people, has approached the womb; he has sat down upon the firm foundation. 2.
Soma is the slayer of demons, the destroyer of demons, the observer of all people, and the seer of all. He is struck with iron and struck with gold;
thus says the Brāhmaṇa: "He presses [the Soma] with golden hands."
With the *droṇa* vessel or with the two pressing-boards, he sits down—that is, he approaches—toward the common place, the womb, the location for pressing.

Be the bestower of wide space, the most generous, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra; bring across the wealth of the patrons. 3. Be the bestower of wide space; be the most generous; the greatest slayer of Vṛtra; bring across the wealth of the patrons. 3.
O Soma, you who are the bestower of wide space, become the supreme giver of riches—
since "veda" and "varivas" are listed among the names for wealth—
and become most bountiful, the greatest of givers.
The quality of being a giver of all is stated here, thus there is no tautology.
O most excellent slayer of Vṛtra, become the supreme destroyer of our enemies.
Furthermore, bestow upon us the wealth (*rādhas*)—the riches—of our wealthy enemies.
1. *ga*-ta-*bha*-tatra; 2. *ga*-prāgupetamāyā; 3.
*ga*-yathārthamāvagrahaṇāt; *ta1*-yathārthamāvāgrahaṇāt; *ta5.6*-bha1*-yathārthamāvāpagrahaṇāt; *bha4*-yathārthamatāpagrahaṇāt.

4. *bha1*-kalaśaviśeṣaṇam; *bha4*-kalaśe-dhiṣavaṇam | Flow toward the feast (*vīti*) of the great gods with the juice (*andhas*), and toward strength (*vāja*) as well as fame (*śrava*). 4. Toward. Great. Of the great. Gods. Feast. With the juice. Toward. Strength. And. Fame. 4. O Soma, you—flow toward (*abhyarṣa*), that is, go toward, the feast (*vīti*) of the great, mighty gods, together with the juice (*andhas*), such as the grain-offering. Furthermore (*uta*), by going toward it, you cause us to attain strength (*vāja*) and fame (*śrava*)—this is the meaning.

Toward you we move; this indeed is our purpose day by day. O Indu, upon you alone are our hopes. (5) O Indu—Soma being prepared in the sacrifices—we move toward you; we approach you. Day after day, that very service to you is our sole purpose; there is no other task for us. Our aspirations and expectations as well are fixed upon you alone, and nowhere else. (16)

The daughter of Sūrya purifies your pressed-out Soma with her eternal, extensive strainer. O Soma, the daughter of Sūrya—the goddess Śraddhā—purifies your flowing Soma with her eternal (*śaśvatā*) and expansive (*tanā*) woolen filter (*vāreṇa*). Thus the Vājasaneyins declare: "Śraddhā is indeed the daughter of Sūrya; Śraddhā purifies him."

In the assembly, at the sacrifice, on the day of the Soma-pressing in heaven—the ten sisters, the fingers, moving along, seize him, this very Soma, for the sake of the drink. *taṃ īm anvīḥ samarye ā gṛbhṇanti yoṣaṇāḥ daśa svasāraḥ pārye divi.* In the assembly (*samarye*), at the common sacrifice (*samanupye yajñe*), on the day of the Soma-pressing (*pārye divi*)—the ten sisters (*yoṣaṇāḥ daśa svasāraḥ*), the fingers (*anvīḥ aṇvyo'ṅgulayaḥ*)—seize (*ā gṛbhṇanti*) him, this very Soma (*tamīṃ tamenaṃ somam*). For "fingers" (*anvayaḥ*) is listed among the names for fingers in the lexicon. They grasp him for the sake of the drink.

The vigorous fingers urge him on; they blow the shining, piercing Bākura. The honey, threefold and warding off [enemies], flows forth. (8) They urge him on—the fingers of the skillful one—toward the place of pressing. Having urged him, they blow upon this Soma, the radiant, piercing Bākura, whose stalks are like those of the *dāti* plant. Although the root *dhamati* is not normally used for the act of pressing, it shall here signify pressing by virtue of its appropriateness. This very substance, the honey consisting of Soma, is threefold, having three locations: the *droṇakalaśa*, the *ādhavanīya*, and the *pūtabhṛt* are the three locations. And it is "warding off" (*vāraṇa*), a repeller of enemies.
The milch-cows indeed mix this Soma, the infant, for Indra as their husband. 9. Toward this [Soma], the Adhvaryu priests and the milch-cows mix it—the Soma, the infant—for Indra as their husband. 9.
1. ta1.5.6-bha1-vābhi;
2. ga-bha—the phrase "by means of the wind... purifies" is absent;
3. ga—reads "purifies."
She constantly purifies—that is, cleanses—with a filter made of wool, a cloth that is constant and firm.
Regarding this, the *Yajurbrāhmaṇa* says: "With a constant [filter] she flows. For it is with a filter that one purifies the Soma; thus it is said, "purifying" (punatī).
[Variant readings: 4. *ga-ta5-aṇvīretā*.]
5. ga—“unlike [anything else] by its rays”; gha—“unlike honey. 6. ga, ta1.2.5.6, bha—“and they press out.
Furthermore, the inviolable cows, the milch-cows, mix this young child, Soma, for Indra to drink. They pour it forth for him to drink.
The meaning is that they consecrate it with their own milk.

In the exhilarations of this [Soma], Indra indeed strikes down all Vṛtras; as a hero, he bestows riches as well. 10. In the exhilarations of this, Indra indeed strikes down all Vṛtras; as a hero, he bestows riches as well. 10.
The heroic Indra, in the exhilaration of this very Soma, strikes down all enemies, every single Vṛtra;
and he bestows riches and wealth upon the sacrificers.
The second hymn, consisting of ten verses beginning with "pavasva," is the seerly composition (*ārṣa*) of Medhātithi Kāṇva and is in the Gāyatrī meter.
It is called "Samudra" (the Ocean).
It is "Samudra" because [the waters] flow from it as an ocean.
The Soma, the supporter of heaven—that is, of the celestial realm—and its sustainer, desiring us, is cleansed within the waters; that is to say, it is purified and poured out into the filter.

The tawny bull has bellowed; great like Mitra, he is beautiful to behold; he shines together with the sun. 6. He has bellowed; the bull; the tawny one; the great; like Mitra; beautiful to behold; together; with the sun; he shines. 6.

The showerer of desires, the golden-hued Hari, the Great One who is supreme over all—like Mitra, a friend, he is beautiful to behold; this Soma who has uttered his sound shines together with the Sun, manifesting in the sky.

O Indra, songs are cleansed by your might; those seekers of the waters adorn themselves with them for your exhilaration. (7) *Giraḥ* | *te* | *indra* | *iti* | *ojasā* | *mamṛjyante* | *apsuyavaḥ* | *yābhiḥ* | *madāya* | *śumbhase* || 7 ||

O Indra, by your *ojas*—your power—those songs of praise (*giraḥ*) seeking the waters, which are connected to ritual action, are cleansed and purified; through those songs, you, flowing forth for exhilaration, adorn yourself and are made beautiful.

We pray to you, the maker of wide space, for the sake of exhilarating joy; there our great praises are proclaimed. 8. We pray to you, the maker of wide space, for the sake of exhilarating joy; there our great praises are proclaimed. 8.

O Soma, for you whose praises are great and exultant, we pray to you—that Soma who, through your grace, creates the highest world—for the sake of exhilaration, for the sacrificer who is by nature a subduer of enemies. We implore you for the sake of intoxication.
For us, O Indu, flow with your stream of honey, seeking Indra, like Parjanya rich in rain. 9. For us; O Indu; seeking Indra; of honey; flow; with your stream; like Parjanya; rich in rain. 9.

O Soma, you who belong to Indra, who desire Indra, flow for us—Medhātithi and his kin—with a stream of sweet, intoxicating nectar; just as Parjanya, the rain-giving cloud, pours down rain, so do you flow and pour forth for us.

O Indu, you are the winner of cattle, the winner of men, the winner of horses, and the winner of booty; you are the primordial soul of the sacrifice. 10. O Indu, you are the winner of cattle, the winner of men, the winner of horses, and the winner of booty; you are the primordial soul of the sacrifice. 10.
O Indra, you are the ancient, primordial soul of the sacrifice; as our protector, you are the one who bestows cattle upon us,
you are the giver of sons,
and you are the giver of horses.
Moreover, you are indeed a winner of prizes and a giver of food.

"This is the god"—this third hymn, consisting of ten verses, has Ājīgarti Śunaḥśepa as its seer, is in the Gāyatrī meter, and has Pavamāna Soma as its deity. It is recorded thus: "Eṣaḥ [is] Śunaḥśepaḥ.
The application (viniyoga) has already been stated.
1. *ta-darśato kaṃ*; bha1.4-*darśato ka* | 2. gha-mu- *saṃ rocate* | 3.
ga-*madakarasya rasasya*; gha-*tava- madakarasya somasya*; ta4-*madakarasyottamasya*; ta5-*madakarasyāmattasya* |
4. Thus the cloud pours forth;

so this immortal god flies like a winged bird to settle within the wooden vats. This god, the immortal one, flies like a winged bird toward the wooden vats to take his seat. This Soma, shining and deathless, flies with speed like a bird toward the *droṇa* vessels for the purpose of settling therein.

This god, prepared by the fingers, runs past the enemies; flowing, he is inviolable. This god, prepared by the fingers—since "fingers" are listed among the names for *vipas* (Atharva Veda)—this Soma, the god being purified and flowing, being inviolable and unharmed by anyone, runs past the enemies (*hrāṃsi*) and rushes toward them to slay them.

This god, being purified by those who praise him and by those who love the Truth, the tawny one, is cleansed for the sake of booty. This god, being purified by those who offer praise and by those who desire the Truth, the tawny one, like a horse, is cleansed with hymns for the sake of booty—that is, for the sake of battle. Being purified and flowing, this Soma, the god, is cleansed through praises by the *vipanyus*, the praisers, and by the *ṛtāyus*, those who desire the sacrifice; he, the tawny one (*hari*), like a horse, is adorned with hymns for the sake of booty (*vāja*).

This hero, flowing forth, as he goes forth with his powers, desires to bestow all desirable treasures. (4) This one—flowing, the hero, the brave, this divine Soma—desires to distribute all desirable riches with his powers, as he moves along, wishing to share them for our sake.

This god, flowing forth, speeds along his chariot; he bestows gifts and makes his voice manifest. (5) This god, flowing forth, speeds along his chariot; he bestows gifts and makes his voice manifest. (5) Flowing and streaming, this Soma, the god, desires a chariot for the sake of coming toward our sacrifice. Having arrived, he bestows upon us what we desire. He makes his voice manifest; being pressed, he reveals his sound. (20)

Praised by the sages, this god plunges into the waters, bestowing treasures upon the donor. (6) This one—praised by the *vipras*, the wise singers, from all sides; this god Soma; plunging into the *apas* (the ritual waters, the *vasatīvarīs*); bestowing—that is, holding and granting—treasures, delightful riches, to the *dāśus*, the sacrificer who offers oblations. (6)

He rushes through the sky across the regions with his stream, being pressed and bellowing loudly. 7. He—through the sky—he rushes; across the regions; with his stream; being pressed; bellowing loudly. 7.
1. *ga*-sutobhiputaḥ; 2. *ga*, *ta*, *bha*, *mu*—*yajñakīrmair vā*; 3. *gha*—*pavamānaḥ pūyamānaḥ*; 4. *ga*, *gha*, *ta*, *bha*—*prayacchati ca*.

Flowing in a stream, this Soma, being purified, roaring as it is pressed, pervading the worlds, speeds forth across the regions toward heaven. This one has spread across heaven, passing through the worlds untouched; purifying himself, he goes to his own sacrifice. This Soma, being purified, flowing, performing the excellent sacrifice, and remaining untouched—unharmed by anyone—speeds forth toward heaven from the sacrifice, passing through the worlds.

This god, pressed for the gods by means of his ancient birth, the tawny one, flows through the filters. 9. This—by means of his ancient—birth—the shining god, pressed for the gods, the tawny one, flows through the filters. 9. *Hariḥ* (tawny) means golden-colored; *devaḥ* (god) means shining; *eṣaḥ* (this) refers to Soma; *pratanena* (ancient) means by his primordial; *janmanā* (birth) means by his origin; *devebhyaḥ* (for the gods) means for the sake of the gods; *sutaḥ* (pressed) means having been extracted; being thus, *pavitraiḥ* (through the filters) he *arṣati* (flows), that is, he goes.

This very one, of many vows, being born, generating nourishments, flows with a stream when pressed. 10. This—*ūm*—this very one, of many vows (*puruvrataḥ*), being born (*jajñānaḥ*), generating (*janayan*) nourishments (*iṣaḥ*), flows (*pavate*) with a stream (*dhārayā*) when pressed (*sutaḥ*). This very one—*syaḥ*—is indeed this Soma, of many vows, performing many deeds; even as he is being born, generating nourishments—that is, producing food—he, having been pressed, flows, that is, he streams forth with a stream. 21.

The fourth hymn, consisting of ten verses beginning with "sanā ca," is the seerly composition (ārṣa) of Hiraṇyastūpa of the Aṅgirasa lineage; it is in the Gāyatrī meter and has Pavamāna Soma as its deity.
It is recorded thus: "sana [is the hymn of] Hiraṇyastūpa.
Its ritual application (viniyoga) has been stated.

Winning, O Soma, and conquering, O Pavamāna, bestow great glory; then, make us more prosperous. Winning, O Soma, and conquering, O Pavamāna, bestow great glory; then, make us more prosperous. O Soma, O Pavamāna, you who possess great glory—win [the gods] for us; grant us our share of the deities worthy of worship. And conquer! Conquer the Rākṣasas who destroy the sacrificial rites. Then, having reached the gods and having conquered the Rākṣasas, make us more prosperous—that is, make us better; give us what is excellent. This is the meaning.

Winning light, winning heaven, and all fortunes, O Soma—make us more prosperous. Winning light; winning heaven; and all fortunes, O Soma—make us more prosperous. O Soma, you, win light—that is, bestow splendor upon us. Moreover, win heaven—that is, grant us the celestial realm. And win all fortunes—that is, bestow all forms of auspiciousness. The rest is self-evident.

Win for us skill and wisdom; O Soma, strike away our enemies, and then make us more prosperous. (3) O Soma, win for us *dakṣa*, strength; and also win for us *kratu*, mental power. Strike away and slay our *mṛdhaḥ*, the harmful enemies. The rest is self-evident.

1. In manuscripts ga, ta, bha, the word ‘tiraḥ’ is absent. 2. In manuscripts ga, gha, ta, bha, ‘uṃ’ is absent. 3. Manuscript ga has ‘sanā’. 4. Manuscripts ta and bha have ‘śreyaḥ’. 5. In manuscripts ga, sa, ma, ‘svaḥ’ is absent.

O purifiers! Purify the Soma for Indra to drink. And make us better off. (4) O purifiers—O you who perform the pressing of the Soma—purify the Soma for Indra to drink; that is, press it out. The rest is established [as in the preceding].

Do thou grant us the sun; do thou [grant it] by thy proper time and by thy protections. Furthermore, make us more prosperous. 5. O Soma, do thou, by thy proper time (*ṛtvan*) and by thy protections (*ūtībhiḥ*)—that is, by the ritual action performed by thee and by the guardianships provided by thee—bestow upon us the sun; cause us to attain it. The rest is established. 22.

Through your wisdom and through your protections, O Soma, may we long behold the sun in heaven; and furthermore, make us more prosperous. *ṛtvā* (through wisdom), *ūtibhiḥ* (through protections), *dyauk* (in heaven), *paśyema* (may we behold), *sūryyam* (the sun). *Artha* (and furthermore), *naḥ* (us), *vasyasaḥ* (more prosperous), *kṛdhi* (make). O Soma, by means of your insight (*ṛtvā*) and by your aids (*ūtibhiḥ*), may we for a long time (*dyauk*) behold the sun (*sūryyam*). We have beheld it, and we shall continue to behold it. The rest is established.

Flow toward us, O Soma of excellent weapons; bring us wealth that is doubly powerful. Furthermore, make us more prosperous. O Soma, you whose weapons are beautiful, flow toward us with wealth that is doubly powerful—that is, abundant in both places, heaven and earth. Bring this wealth to us. The rest is already established.

Flow toward us with wealth, unshaken in battles, victorious; bring us to greater prosperity. (8) O Soma, in battles—unshaken by enemies, invincible, and the overcomer of foes—you flow toward us; bring us wealth and lead it to us. The rest is established.

They have magnified you with sacrifices, O Pavamāna, in the support of the world; therefore, make us more prosperous. (9) O Pavamāna Soma, for the sake of supporting the sacrificers, they—the sacrificers—have magnified you with sacrifices in the support of the world, that is, for the purpose of their own support. The rest is self-evident.

O Indu, bring us wonderful wealth, accompanied by horses and full of life; then, make us more prosperous. 10. Wealth for us—wonderful, with horses, O Indu, bringing all life—bring it hither! And then, make us more prosperous. 10.

*tara-aiśyāmaḥ* is absent.

O *Indu*, Soma who is being moistened in the sacrifices, bring to us—that is, fetch for us—the wonderful, manifold, horse-drawn chariot (*aśvinam*) that possesses horses, and which is all-pervading (*viśvāyum*).
The rest is self-evident.
The fifth hymn, consisting of eleven verses beginning with "samiddhaḥ," belongs to Asita Devala Kāśyapa and is composed in the *ṛṣabha* meter.
Of these, the eight verses from the eighth onwards are *anuṣṭubh*s, while the remaining seven are *gāyatrī*s.
With the exception of the verse dedicated to Narāśaṃsa, the deities for each successive verse are, in order, Samit and the others.

And thus it has been listed: “*Samiddha* [consists of] eleven [verses]; [the seers are] Kāśyapa, Asita, or Devala; there are twenty hymns (*sūkta*s); the first is an *Āprī* hymn ending in a *triṣṭubh*.
This *Āprī* hymn of Kāśyapa belongs to the *pāvamāna* [section].
And it is prescribed in the Sūtra: “*Samiddho adya* [is used] for all [seers], or according to the respective ṛṣi” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 1.2).

Kindled, the Lord from every side, flowing forth, he shines resplendent; the bull, bellowing loudly, brings delight. || 1 || Kindled, the Lord from every side, flowing forth, he shines resplendent; the bull, bellowing loudly, brings delight. || 1 ||
The praise of Soma is here without a neck.

Kindled—that is, perfectly ignited—the Lord of All, the Master from every side, the Bull who showers down desires, Soma the Purifier, bellowing—making sound while being pressed—delighting the gods, he shines forth; he manifests in the sacrifices.

Tanūnapāt, being sharpened at his horns, moves along, shining brightly through the mid-air. 2. Tanūnapāt; being sharpened; at his two horns; sharpening; he moves; through the mid-air; shining brightly. 2.
Tanūnapāt is Soma Pavamāna.
In that context, Soma becomes Tanūnapāt.
And thus it is heard in scripture: "From Agni horses are born; from them Soma is born."
Upon the blazing peak, that is, on the elevated region—
for the root *haṇ* is read in the list of blazing *sāman*-verses as "peaks"—
sharpening [his horns], he moves, that is, he hastens through the intermediate space.
He goes toward the *droṇakalaśa*.
And thus it is known: "One draws the *āgrayaṇa* with two streams."

Worthy of praise, flowing forth, the radiant wealth shines intensely with the streams of honey by his might. 3. Worthy of praise, flowing forth, the radiant wealth shines intensely with the streams of honey by his might. 3.

Soma Pavamāna, worthy of praise and hymns, the giver of desired wealth, being resplendent and luminous, shines forth and manifests with power and strength as he flows along with the streams of honeyed water.

Spreading the sacrificial grass eastward with vigor, the flowing Soma, the tawny one, moves as a god among the gods. 4. *Barhiḥ* (the sacrificial grass), *prācīnam* (eastward), *ojasā* (with vigor), *pavamānaḥ* (the flowing one), *stṛṇan* (spreading), *hariḥ* (the tawny one), *deveṣu* (among the gods), *devaḥ* (the god), *īyate* (moves). 4.
Hari, the golden-hued god, the shining Soma, being purified, goes with vigor and power, spreading the sacrificial grass (barhis) with its tips directed eastward among the gods at the sacrifices.
1. You are the one who has taken up the burden; you are the one who has [taken up] the burden. 2. Of the one who was attended by Kāśyapa, who had gone to the fourth stage. 3. The Nārāśaṃsa hymn.
4. *ga*: This is the Pavamāna Soma of Śaunaka; *ta-bha4*: This is the Pāvamāna of Śaunaka.
5. *ta-bha4*: Āprīta Soma; *su*: Āpriya Soma. 6. *gha*: Tanūnapāt Deva.

7. Regarding the entry into the *ta* [vessel]. 8. According to the *ga*, the *āgrayaṇa* [is drawn] with the two *parā*; according to *ta6*, the *āgrayaṇa* with the two *āsā*; according to *bhara.3*, the *āgrayaṇa*. 9.

10. The word *ga-ta-bha4* meaning "among the gods" does not exist.

The golden, divine doors open wide, exalted by the one being purified; they have been well-praised by the singers. (5) The golden, divine doors—golden (*hiraṇyayīḥ*), the doors that are goddesses (*dvāro devīḥ*)—well-praised (*suṣṭutāḥ*) along with the flowing Soma (*pavamānena*), immediately open wide (*ud...jihate*) from the vast, lofty directions (*bṛhad āttaiḥ*). For "the *ātā*s" are listed among the names for the quarters of space. They rise up (*ut...jihate*). (24)

The two well-fashioned, vast, and great ones—the Night and Dawn—are being pressed out; they desire the rain-god, for they are beautiful to behold. (6) "Suśilpe" means "well-fashioned. "Bṛhatī" means "vast. "Mahī" means "great. "Parvamānaḥ" refers to the one being pressed. "Vṛṣaṇyati" means "he desires the rain-god. "Naktoṣāsā" refers to "Night and Dawn. "Na" means "not. "Darśyate" means "they are visible. Thus: "The two well-fashioned, beautiful, vast, and great ones—Night and Dawn—are not [yet] fully visible, yet they are worthy of being seen. (6)

O Pavamāna Soma, anoint with a stream of honey the Lord of the Forest (vanaspati), who is green-hued, golden, shining, and possessed of a thousand branches. O Pavamāna Soma, you who are green-colored and at times golden-hued, anoint—that is, prepare—the Lord of the Forest, who is shining, possessing a thousand branches, green, and golden, with a stream consisting of honey. The root *añj* here has the sense of "preparation" (*saṃskṛti*).

O All-Gods (Viśve Devāḥ), Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Sūrya, Agni, and Indra, come together in harmony to the Svāhā-call of the purifying Soma. O All-Gods, Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Sūrya, Agni, and Indra—come all of you, being of one accord, to the Svāhā-call of the purifying Soma; come hither! (11)
The sixth hymn, consisting of nine verses beginning with "mandrayā," belongs to Asita Kāśyapa or to the god [Soma]; it is in the Gāyatrī meter and has Pavamāna Soma as its deity.

O Soma, flow with a pleasant stream as a bull, seeking the gods; another [stream], seeking us, flows through the sheep's wool. O Soma, as a bull—the showerer of desires—seeking the gods and seeking us, flow with a pleasant, intoxicating stream through the sheep's wool, that is, through the strainer of the fleece. Flow forth!

Flow toward that exhilarating, intoxicating joy, O Indu; flow toward the prize-winning steeds. O Indu, Soma—considering you to be Indra, the Lord—flow toward that exhilarating, intoxicating joy; flow toward the prize-winning, powerful horses for our sake.

Flowing forth, being pressed, flow toward that ancient exhilarating draught in the filter; flow toward strength and fame. O Soma, being pressed—that is, being extracted—you, flowing toward that ancient, well-known exhilarating draught—the juice that causes intoxication—flow completely into the filter. Flow toward us with strength (vāja); and furthermore, bestow upon us renown (śravas), which is food.

Having passed through the ten-fibered filter (*daśāpavitra*), that Soma which is sporting—that is, moving about—in the wood, meaning in the forest; him, the ten women—the fingers, as the meaning is—[grasp].
Thus, there is another Vedic verse: "The ten women, the fingers, grasp him who is capable" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 9.1.7).
They groom and attend to him who is vigorous and strong, like a courser, like a horse;
this is connected with the following [verse].

Mix that bull-like juice with milk for exhilaration, for the feast of the gods, and for the sake of the prize-winning chariot. 6. Mix that bull-like juice with milk for exhilaration, for the feast of the gods, and for the sake of the prize-winning chariot. 6.
Mix together—that is, join with milk and juices—that pressed juice, the showerer of desires, for the feast of the gods, for their drinking and exhilaration; mix it for the sake of the battle.

The god, being pressed, flows clear for the god Indra to sustain; when his milk causes him to swell. 7. God, for the god, to be sustained, for Indra he flows, being pressed; when his milk has caused him to swell. 7.
For the shining god Indra, the pressed juice—the shining divine Soma—is purified; that is, it flows in a stream.
Because his milk has nourished Indra—that is, because it has satisfied him—therefore he flows in a stream. This is the meaning.

The self of the sacrifice, pressed with skill, flows as the extracted juice; he guards the ancient work. 8. The self of the sacrifice, with speed, being well-pressed, flows as the extracted juice; he protects the ancient deed. 8.
The soul of the sacrifice, having been prepared, the pressed Soma, being purified, flows forth with great speed, impelling the desires of the sacrificer;
he protects and preserves his own ancient poetic wisdom.

Thus, being purified, seeking Indra, you have placed within the secret cave the most intoxicating exhilaration for the feast and our songs of praise. 9. Thus | purifying | seeking Indra | exhilaration | most intoxicating | for the feast | even in the secret cave | you have placed | our songs. 9.
O most intoxicating Soma, you who bring great exhilaration and desire for Indra, flow thus as you purify yourself for the sake of Indra’s drinking; while streaming into the secret place—
that is, into the sacrificial hall—
you take up even the songs, the very sounds [of praise].
At the time of the pressing, you hold [the Soma] over the sounding-holes;
the meaning is that you perform [this act].

It is introduced with the word "Asugram. Asita Devala is the seer (*ṛṣi*). Both of them belong to the Kaśyapa lineage. Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*). Pavamāna Soma is the deity (*devatā*). The drops of Soma, possessing beautiful support, knowing the connection of this [Indra], flow forth by the path of the rite of Truth along the way of the Law. Beautifully supported (suśriyaḥ), knowing the connection (yojanam)—that is, the relationship—with this Indra, the drops (indavaḥ), the Somas, knowing the path (pathā) of the rite (dharman) of Truth (ṛtasya), are released by the way of the sacrifice (yajñasya). They flow forth (asugram) toward the desirable (sugram). (Note: The commentary clarifies that *suśriyaḥ* means "having beautiful support" (*śobhana-śrayaṇāḥ*), and that they know the connection with Indra; *dharman* refers to the ritual action (*karmani*); *ṛtasya* refers to the sacrifice (*yajñasya*); and *asugram* indicates they are being poured forth.)

He is the Soma, the sacrificial essence. 2.

The foremost, the bull, has bellowed down into the wood; the true sacrifice, with its navel firmly set, [has come]. When the Seer—Soma, whose deeds are far-reaching—clothing himself in *nṛmṇā*, that is, manly powers or riches, and enveloping himself in *kāvyā*, that is, poetic wisdoms or the hymns which are the works of seers, moves around (*pari arpati*) when he goes forth, then the swift one (*vājī*), Indra, desires to win the light of heaven (*svar*). He wishes to gather his own strength in order to return toward the sacrifice.

O you two, Rodasī (Heaven and Earth), for the sake of winning (*sātaye*) the sweet Soma-natured food (*vāja*) that delights the gods, grant to us—those who are worthy of the Kāvyas or the descendants of Kāvya—the wealth (*rayi*), fame (*śravaḥ*), and food (*anna*), as well as other desirable things such as cattle and other riches; conquer them completely!
That is to say, bestow them upon us.
‘ete somāḥ’ (These Soma-libations) is the eighth hymn, consisting of nine verses. The seer and other details are as before. And it is enumerated thus: ‘ete somāḥ’.
The application of the hymns has been stated.

Regarding the pressing-stone praise (*grāvastotra*), according to the opinion of Gāṇagāri, when the Soma is being cleansed during the preparation of the suitable [vessel], the verse “They cleanse thee” (*mṛjanti tvā*) is used.

And it is sūtra-ed: “Now he should perform another suitable [rite]; thus says Gāṇagāri: ‘Swell up, let [the milk] come to thee’—these three verses; ‘Thee the ten fingers cleanse’” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 5.12).

These Soma juices have flowed toward the beloved desire of Indra, increasing his heroic power. 1. These: Soma juices; toward; the beloved; of Indra; the desire; have flowed; increasing; his; heroic power. 1.

These Soma juices, having been pressed, increasing Indra’s heroism and power, have flowed toward, are being poured out toward, and have rained down upon his desirable, beloved, and delightful essence.

Being purified, seated in the vessels, and going toward Vāyu and the Aśvins—may they bestow upon us great heroic strength. || 2 || Being purified; seated in the vessels; going; toward Vāyu; the two Aśvins; they; for us; may they bestow; great heroic strength. || 2 ||

that is to say, may they grant it.

The ten fingers cleanse you; the seven prayers impel you. The wise have rejoiced after you. And the wise (*viprāḥ*), the inspired ones, have rejoiced after you, celebrating you in succession.

The sage, the son of Heaven, being pressed, goes forth toward his beloved [abodes], placed between the two granddaughters [of Heaven]—he who possesses the wisdom of a seer.

The poet, the wise one, possessing the insight of a seer—one whose wisdom has reached its limit or whose action has reached its limit—is Soma. Placed upon, that is, deposited within, the two granddaughters, the two pressing-boards, being pressed—that is, being extracted—he has reached from heaven, from the world of light, his most beloved branches.
Thus says a Vedic verse: "Like falcons, you have passed beyond the branches of the mountains.
He goes; he moves.

O Soma, flow forth abundantly for your own dwelling, for the benevolent and non-malicious praiseworthy person who offers praise, for the sake of enjoyment and consumption; being well-pleased and sufficient, flow with your most excellent stream toward the sacrifice.
He, the pure son, as soon as he was born, caused his two parents who were already born to shine; he, the great one, [caused] the two great ones, the increasers of Truth (Ṛta), to shine.

Born, arisen, pure, purified, great, the supreme oblation—that son named Soma—caused the two vast ones, the increasers of cosmic order (*ṛtāvṛdhā*), the two mothers who are the generators of all that is born, namely Heaven and Earth, to shine; he makes them radiant, he illumines them.

Resounding like chariots, like neighing horses seeking glory, the Soma drops have flowed forth for the sake of wealth. Resounding—making sound in the sounding-holes at the time of the pressing—the Soma drops, like chariots making noise, or like neighing horses making noise, being seekers of fame (*śravasyavaḥ*)—desiring food from their enemies—have flowed forth for the sake of wealth, that is, for the riches of the sacrificers; they have come.

Being urged forth like chariots, they have been placed within the two hands, like the burdens of craftsmen. The Soma juices are anointed with praises, as kings are with eulogies; they are anointed with milk products, as the sacrifice is by the seven officiating priests. The pressed drops, being purified for exhilaration by the prayer and the song, flow forth in a stream once they have been extracted. Soma, being purified, flows in a thousand streams through the sheep’s wool—past the filter—to the prepared place of Vāyu and Indra. This purifying, cleansing Soma flows; what kind of Pavamāna is he? He is "thousand-streamed," possessing immeasurable streams, and "past the sheep's wool. Here, by the word *avi*, its wool is meant; the meaning is that he passes through the *daśāpavitra* (the ten-strand filter) produced from sheep's wool. He goes "past" (*ati*) it. For what purpose? It is understood: for the drinking of Vāyu and Indra. Toward what? Toward the "prepared place" (*niṣkṛtam*). In this sense, *niṣkṛta* means "well-prepared"; toward the consecrated vessel.

Alternatively, the word "with golden ones" (*rukmibhiḥ*) may also be an adjective qualifying the rays themselves. Men cleanse him who is to be cleansed, as he prepares great nourishments, within the wooden vats. Men—meaning human beings, the officiating priests—cleanse this Soma, who is worthy of being cleansed, as they press him. Where? Within the *droṇa* vessels, that is, the *droṇakalaśa* jars. Of what sort is he? He is one who prepares great nourishments (*mahīriṣaḥ*), meaning he performs great sacrifices; the sense is that he yields abundant juices. In the *Grāvastotṛ* litany, according to the opinion of Gāṇagāri, when the Soma is being cleansed during the preparatory rite, this verse "etamu tyam" is used. It is also prescribed in the Sūtra: "etamu tyaṃ daśa kṣipo mṛjyamānaḥ suhastyā" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 5.12).

Ten fingers and seven priests cleanse this very one—the well-armed, most exhilarating [Soma]. Of what nature is he? Well-armed (*svāyudham*)—possessing beautiful weapons—and most exhilarating (*madintamam*), the greatest of intoxicators. The mention of the word "well-armed" is for the purpose of demonstrating his capacity for slaying demons. He who holds within his two hands all desirable treasures—you are the bestower of everything in the exhilarations [of the Soma]. *Yaḥ somaḥ viśvāni vāryā vasūni hastayoḥ ā dadhe, madeṣu sarvadhāḥ asi.* That Soma who places all desirable (*vārya*) treasures (*vasūni*) into the hands of the worshipper—meaning he bestows them—is "the giver of all" (*sarvadhāḥ*) in the exhilarations (*madeṣu*). Alternatively, this connects with the word *sa śuṣmī* (he, the powerful one) in the following verse.

He who milks these two great worlds together like a mother and a father—O Soma, in your exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things. *Yaḥ*, *ime*, *rodasī*, *mahī*, *sam*, *mātarā-iva*, *dohate*, *madeṣu*, *sarvadhaḥ*, *asi*. That Soma milks these two great *rodasī*, heaven and earth, together; that is to say, he gathers the essence of both. Just as a single calf might milk both mothers together, so it is.

Among the exhilarating draughts, having drunk of that Soma which is pre-eminently intoxicating, Indra, being irresistible (*apratigataḥ*), struck down (*jaghāna*)—that is, he slew—the Vṛtras, the enemies. And "now" (*nu*) means swiftly; he strikes them down, and let him strike them even at this very moment. The twenty-seventh hymn begins with "pra somāsaḥ. Asita Devala is the seer, the Gāyatrī is the metre, and Soma is the deity. This is indicated by the phrase "pra somāsaḥ. The application (*viniyoga*) has been explained.

The Soma drops have flowed forth, the flowing drops; being mixed with milk, they are cleansed in the waters. The Soma drops have flowed forth, the flowing drops; being mixed with milk, they are cleansed in the waters. The *somāsas* (Somas), the *pavamānāsas* (flowing/purifying) *indavas* (drops), radiant, have *prādhanviṣuḥ*—the root *dhanvati* meaning "to go"—they go forth. Furthermore, *śrīṇānāḥ*, being mixed with milk, they *mṛñjata*, they are cleansed in the *apsu* (waters), namely the *vasatīvarīs*.

The cows have flowed forth; like waters going down a steep descent, the purifying drops have reached Indra. The cows—the moving drops—have flowed toward [the filter]. What is it like? Like waters going down a steep descent (*pravat*), they have gone. Then, being purified, they have reached Indra to please him; or rather, through the channel of the oblation, they have pervaded Indra himself.

Flow forth, O Pavamāna Soma; run for Indra to drink, as you are led away by the men. 3 O Pavamāna Soma, you run forth toward the Āhavanīya fire from the *havirdhāna* shed for Indra to drink. This is what is meant: being guided and led by the men—the leaders, the priests—you are brought forth from the *havirdhāna*. Alternatively: O Pavamāna, you run forth toward the vessel for Indra’s drinking; for that purpose, you are led down from the *havirdhāna*.

You, who are a pure friend and worthy of joyful praise—that is, worthy of hymns—flow. This is the syntactical connection.

O Indu, when, pressed by the stones, you run around the filter, you are sufficient for the abode of Indra. O Indu, when—pressed by the stones, that is, extracted—you run around the filter, which is the *daśāpavitra*, you then become sufficient (*aram*) for the abode (*dhāman*) of Indra; that is, for his place, his support, or his vessel.

Flow forth, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra, to be celebrated with hymns—pure, purifying, and wonderful. Flow forth as one of such magnificent power.

Pure, purifying, he is called Soma, the pressed sweet juice; the one who favors the gods and slays the wicked. (7) Pure, purifying, he is called Soma, the pressed sweet juice; the one who favors the gods and slays the wicked. (7) The Soma, which is the essence of the pressed (*sutasya*) sweet (*madhvaḥ*) intoxicating draught, is itself pure (*śuciḥ*) and is called purifying (*pāvakaḥ*). Likewise, he is the one who favors the gods (*devāvīḥ*), meaning the one who gratifies the gods, and the slayer of the wicked (*aghaśaṃsahā*). Those who proclaim evil (*agham*) or sin are the *aghaśaṃsāḥ*, namely the Asuras; he is said to be their destroyer. In the second Anuvāka there are thirty-six hymns. Among them, the first hymn, beginning with "Parvasva," is a prose-like composition. It is the seerhood of Daḷahacyuta, the son of Agastya, and is in the Gāyatrī meter, dedicated to the deity Pavamāna Soma. It is recorded thus: "Parvasva: six [verses]; Daḷahacyuta, [the seer] of Agastya. The application (*viniyoga*) has been explained.

Flow forth, O Soma, who art the accomplisher of strength; flow for the drinking of the gods, O golden-hued one, as a gladdening draught for the Maruts and for Vāyu. Flow forth, O accomplisher of strength (*dakṣasādhana*). For the drinking of the gods—of Indra and the others—O golden-hued (*hara*) remover of sin, flow! Flow as a gladdening draught (*mada*) that produces exhilaration, for the Maruts and for Vāyu as well, for their drinking. Flow forth.

O Pavamāna, placed by the prayer (dhiyā) or by our ritual action, crying out loudly toward your womb (yoni), enter Vāyu according to the law (dharmaṇā). This third hymn, consisting of six verses beginning with "eṣa kaviḥ," is the seer-poem (ārṣa) of Numedhas, the son of Aṅgiras; it is in the Gāyatrī meter and dedicated to Soma.

The ritual application (viniyoga) has been stated.

This sage, shaken by the fingers, flows over the filter; being purified, he strikes down the adversaries. (1) This one—the Soma—is the sage, the wise one. Shaken all around, praised on every side, he flows over the filter—that is, across the ten-strand woolen filter (*daśāpavitra*). Although the root *tośati* denotes the act of killing, here, because there is a sense of movement involved in the striking, it functions in the sense of motion; the meaning is "he goes. Alternatively, he flows over the filter—that is, upon the black antelope skin (*kṛṣṇājina*)—he is struck; the meaning is that he is pressed. What is he doing? Being purified, being cleansed, he strikes down—that is, drives away—the adversaries, the enemies.

Into the wooden vessels (vaneṣu)—those desirable objects or the cups made from the wood of the *vana* tree. He is the knower of all (viśvavit); such is the connection. Desiring cattle, desiring gold, this Indu, being purified, has bellowed. He is the ever-conquering, the invincible. This Soma, being purified, has bellowed. Being of what nature? Being purified, he laughs with the Sun above the sky, in the filter, he the exhilarating, intoxicating draught. Although the Soma is cast into the filter held in the hands today, the thought is that he is nevertheless cast into the filter by the Sun in the intermediate region, for the sake of his power. One should not ask, "What concern has the Sun with the flowing of Soma among other gods? for the Soma is nourished by the very rays of the Sun. This steed, urged by the men, the knower of all, the lord of the mind, runs through the sheep's wool filter. Such as he is, he, the one to be approached, repeatedly cleanses himself through the filter of the *vāra*—that is, the *darbha* grass—and flows forth, moving in various ways.

it streams while entering—that is, penetrating—all the *dhāman*s, meaning all the divine bodies.

The fifth hymn, consisting of six verses beginning with "grāmya," is the seerage of Nṛmedha Āṅgirasa; it is in the Gāyatrī meter and has Pavamāna Soma as its deity. It is enumerated thus: "Prāsya nṛmedhaḥ. The application (viniyoga) has already been explained.
His streams have flowed forth by the power of the pressed-out bull, as he stands ready to serve the gods. 1. The streams of this pressed-out bull have flowed forth by his might, serving the gods. 1.

Of this Soma, the bull, the showerer, who has been pressed, purified, and who desires to prevail over the gods, seeking to manifest his power through his own vigor, the streams have flowed forth—they flow forth preeminently.

The two wise singers, chanting with their song, release the steed Ga-gha-ta-bha-mu-drumaya; they release the steed, the light that has been born, worthy of praise. The wise singers, chanting with their song, release the steed—the light that has been born, worthy of praise.
They release—that is, they purify—the *soma*, which is like a steed (*aśva*) or whose very nature is to flow (*sarpaṇa*).
Who are they? The singers (*kāravaḥ*), the performers of ritual acts such as the *adhvaryu*s, who are "ordainers" (*vedhasaḥ*) and "praisers" (*gṛṇantaḥ*).
By means of "speech"—that is, by means of praise as an instrument—[he attains] the steed.
Of what kind?
The steed is "light," the shining Soma, who is "being born."
The meaning is "increased.
Alternatively, it refers to the light being born, according to the Vedic revelation: "This Soma is indeed the light";
and "ukthya" means "praiseworthy."
With thy beautiful rays, O Soma, as thou art being purified for us, O Lord of abundant wealth, increase the ocean that is worthy of praise. || 3 ||
O Soma, O Lord of abundant wealth (*prabhūtavasu*), those splendors of yours, which are beautiful and victorious, belong to you as you are being purified while already pure.
Since this is so, therefore, increase—that is, fill with essence—that *ukthya* (worthy of praise) vessel, the *droṇakalaśa*, which is like the ocean. Fill it with juice.
Conquering all realms, flow forth, O Soma, with your stream; drive away our enemies completely. 4. All realms. Conquering. Flow forth. O Soma. With your stream. Drive away. Enemies. Completely. 4.
O Soma, conquering all treasures for our sake, flow forth; stream with your current.
Drive away all hateful enemies simultaneously toward distant lands.

Protect us well from the roar of every single ruddy one; protect us where we may be released from reproach. 5. Protect | well | us | O ruddy one | from the roar | of every | one | from reproach | where | we may be released. 5.

O Soma, protect us—well, indeed, guard and preserve us—from what? From the roar, the sound of the stingy one, which takes the form of censure. Is it from the stinginess of only one person? No; from that of "every" (samasya) one who exists, from anyone at all; the meaning is, without releasing anyone. Not only from the roar of the stingy one, but rather, protect us from the censure of "anyone" whatsoever who reviles us. Protect us by that protection through which we might be liberated—at whatever moment we may become free.

O Indu, flow with your stream, bestowing earthly and celestial wealth; bring hither resplendent vigor. 6. O Indu, flow with your stream, bestowing earthly and celestial wealth; bring hither resplendent vigor. 6.
O Indu, O Soma, as you are being pressed, flow forth with your stream; pour out from every side.
Bring to us the earthly and celestial wealth, the radiant splendor, and the powerful strength. Bring these to us!

The Indu, being urged by the pressers and being cleansed, bellowing loudly, sends forth the wealth-bringing, Indra-related power. This radiant Indu, the Soma, being urged—that is, being set in motion and occupied with activity—by whom? For what purpose? For Indra’s drinking (*pītaye*). 5.

Press out for Indra, the one who acts with vigor, the Soma most rich in sweetness; press it out, beautiful and exhilarating, for our strength. The hymn beginning with “pra somāsaḥ” consists of six verses; it is the seerly composition (ārṣa) of Iyāvāśva, the son of Atri, and is in the Gāyatrī meter dedicated to Soma.
It is enumerated as follows: “pra somāsaḥ; Iyāvāśva.”
The application is concluded.

The Soma juices, distilling exhilaration, have gone forth for the glory of our liberal patron; pressed for the assembly, they have moved forward. The Soma juices, distilling exhilaration—having been pressed—have gone forth for the glory and nourishment (or fame) of me, the liberal patron, at the sacrificial assembly. They move forward.

Then the maidens of Trita impel the tawny one with the stones—the bright drop for Indra to drink. Then indeed, the maidens of Trita impel this tawny-colored Soma with the pressing-stones. Why? To impel the radiant Indu, the Soma, for Indra’s drinking.

Like a swan entering a flock, he has caused the devotion of everyone to resound; like a steed, he is anointed with milk. 3. And furthermore, just as a swan enters a flock (of birds) by means of its specific flight or its cry, so too does this Soma cause the *mati*—the praise or the intellect—of the entire host of worshippers to resound, bringing it under his control. And that Soma, like a steed (*atya*), is anointed—that is, sprinkled or made glossy—with *gobhiḥ*, meaning with products of the cow or with waters.

Beholding both [worlds], O Soma, like a swift deer you hasten toward the seat of Ṛta. Where? Toward the seat, the place of Ṛta, the sacrifice, sitting upon it, that is, taking your resort. The meaning is: "I go for the sake of accomplishing the sacrifice."

O Soma, bestow upon us—upon us who are generous patrons of the sacrificial offering (maghavadbhyas), and upon us who are great chanters of praise (maha)—splendid, radiant glory and food. Grant it! To what kind of us? To those of us who are generous with oblations and great in our performance of hymns.
Alternatively, "mahyam" means "to me" and "asmabhyam" means "to us.

Since there is no difference in the aspiration for those very [beings] expressed as "asme" (for us) and "maghavadbhyaḥ" (for the liberal patrons), the word "ca" (and) is appropriately used in both cases.

The Soma juices, the wise ones, flow forth like waves of water, like buffaloes toward the forests. 1. The Soma juices, the wise ones, flow forth like waves of water, like buffaloes toward the forests. 1.
The wise, intelligent Soma-drops go forth, they proceed toward the vessels; like what? Like the waves of the waters.
Just as they leap up continuously, so it is here.
This illustration has been shown regarding abundance; another illustration for the act of going is now stated:
like full-grown buffaloes in the forests, like deer.
Alternatively, the first two examples refer to falling from one's own support, while the second refers to descending below the *daśāpavitra*.

Toward the wooden vats, O you who are heard afar, the bright ones have flowed with the stream of Truth—toward the prize consisting of cattle. 2. Toward the wooden vats; O you who are heard afar; the bright ones; with the stream of Truth; toward the prize; consisting of cattle; they have flowed. 2.

The word "flow toward" (abhi kṣaranti) is to be supplied as the remainder [of the sentence]. Because of the presence of the prefix (upasarga), the appropriate verb is to be supplied. "Toward the droṇas" means toward the droṇakalaśa jars.
Although the *droṇakalaśa* is indeed only one, nevertheless, due to the practice of pluralizing for honorific purposes, the others—the *pātrī* and the *droṇas*—are also referred to as such.
Or rather, the plural is used even for a single object for the sake of veneration. Which ones?
The Soma juices are bountiful, tawny-colored, bright, and radiant;
in what manner?
By means of the stream of *ṛta*, that is, by way of a continuous flow of immortality.
Moreover, they flow—that is, they pour forth—vāja, food, accompanied by cattle, meaning abounding in many cows.
Or rather, it is a single sentence:
the Soma juices described above have flowed toward the wooden vats in a stream.
What are they doing?
The meaning is: bestowing cattle-rich booty.

The great ones (*yahnīḥ*), impelled by the Brahman, the mothers (*mātaraḥ*) of the sacrifice (*vṛtasya yajñasya*), the praises (*stutayaḥ*) worthy of being measured out (*nimāṃmyaḥ*), have praised (*abhi...vanuṣata*). "Yahnīḥ" is a name for the great. They praise him.
What?
From heaven— that is, from the deity Heaven— they cleanse and release that very Soma, who stands in the place of a child.
His state as a child of the sky is established by such scriptural passages as: "In this third heaven from here, Soma was" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 3.5.7.1).
O Soma, flow for us from every side, bringing four oceans of wealth, thousandsfold. 6. O Soma, flow for us from every side, bringing four oceans of wealth, thousandsfold. 6.
O Soma, flow forth for our sake from all sides— meaning, flow toward us from every direction— toward those four oceans that are the binders of wealth, which are full of riches; likewise,
pour forth and bestow upon us thousands of immeasurable desires.

Since it is impossible to obtain the specific wealth situated within the four oceans without possessing the land located therein, the sacrificer aspires precisely to the lordship over the entire circle of the earth sealed by the four oceans.

The drop, Soma—being pressed, being poured out, being urged on by the *adhvaryu* priest—flows forth in a continuous stream through the filter. Now it is described directly:
having struck down the sons of the enemy with its vigor and strength, it breaks them apart, shatters them, and scatters them.
Pressed for Indra, for Vāyu, for Varuṇa, and for the Maruts, Soma flows for Viṣṇu. 2. Pressed—for Indra—for Vāyu—for Varuṇa—for the Maruts—Soma—flows—for Viṣṇu. 2.

They press the bull-like Soma with stones, which is joined with the showerers; they milk the milk by means of their skill. He becomes the youth of Trita; he becomes the exhilarating one for Indra. The tawny one is anointed with forms. Likewise, he becomes the youth for Indra, for Indra’s drinking. And the tawny-colored Soma is thoroughly anointed with forms—that is, with substances such as milk and the like.

The sons of Pṛśni milk out for him the world of Truth—that which is beautiful, most dear, and the oblation. (5) *Abhīm*—for him; *ṛtasya viṣṭapam*—the realm of Truth; that is to say, the support of the sacrifice. The *pṛśnimātaraḥ* (sons of Pṛśni), namely the Maruts, *abhiduhte* (milk out) such a thing. What? The *priyatamam* (most dear) *haviḥ* (oblation)—the means of offering—which is *cāru* (beautiful) and *manoharam* (delightful) to Indra and the other gods. For through the rain impelled by the Maruts, there is an increase of Soma; therefore, they have rejoiced.

The hymn beginning with "pra naḥ" is the twentieth, consisting of six verses; it is the seerly composition (ārṣa) of Ayāsya Āṅgirasa, composed in the Gāyatrī metre, and has Pavamāna Soma as its deity.

O Indu, bearing your wave like a flood, flow forth for our great extension toward the gods, you who are tireless. || 1 ||
O Soma, you, being pressed, go forth toward us for our great acquisition of wealth.
This tireless seer, bearing and holding your wave—your surge—proceeds toward the gods to sacrifice.

Praised by mortals, impelled by prayer, Soma flows toward the one who hastens; the sage, with his stream, acts as a skillful craftsman. 2. Praised by mortals, impelled by prayer, Soma flows toward the one who hastens; the sage, with his stream, acts as a skillful craftsman. 2.

Soma, whose action is manifest, is pleased by the hymn—the mental product—of the wise singer; he is served by the prayer, established through ritual action, and set in the sacrifice at a distance, in the region of the filter, where he flows forth, being impelled by his stream.

This one, watchful among the gods, goes pressed into the filter; Soma, the observer of men, moves along. 3. This one, watchful among the gods, goes pressed into the filter; Soma, the observer of men, moves along. 3.
Vigilant and ever-watchful, this Soma, pressed for the sake of the gods, comes hither; it flows everywhere.

Flow for us, seeking strength, performing the beautiful sacrifice; he who possesses the sacred grass invites [the gods] hither. 4. He; for us; flow; seeking strength; performing; beautiful; sacrifice; possessing the sacred grass; hither; invites. 4.

O Soma, you whom the priest holding the sacrificial grass (barhis) seeks to win over and serves—that you, desiring strength (vāja) and seeking food for our sake, flow and pour forth, making this sacrifice free from injury and beautiful and auspicious.
May he, the Soma who possesses inspired heroes and ever-increases us, lead us among the gods for our good fortune and for Vāyu. || 5 ||

This Soma, being purified, for the sake of Vāyu—the deity Vāyu—and for the sake of Bhaga—the deity Bhaga—being a heroic sage impelled by sages who are wise, ever-increasing and eternally growing, shall bestow upon us wealth established among the gods; let him grant it.
1. *gha-ta6-bha1*: You go quickly. 2. *ga*: A praiser. 3. *ga*: One who sees clearly. 4. *gha-ta-bha*: And sacrifice. 5. *bha1*: Always eternally pure; *bhara*: Eternal Brahman.

May he, the knower of seasons, the best finder of the path, win for us today great fame and strength for the sake of obtaining wealth. O Soma, you who know the seasons—the performer of rites—and who are the supreme finder of the way to the holy worlds, on this very day, for our acquisition of riches, conquer great renown, food, and power. This hymn consisting of six verses, beginning with "sa pavasva," is the twenty-first [sūkta]. The seer and other details are as before. It is listed as "sa pavasva. Flow on for exhilaration, O Soma, you who behold men, for the feast of the gods, O Indu, for Indra’s drinking. O Indu, O Soma, you who are the beholder of men—that is, the observer of those who lead—flow on so as to bring happiness for the feast of the gods, for the drinking of Indra, and for exhilaration. Flow, that is, pour forth.

Flow toward our mission as a messenger; you pour yourself out for Indra. From the gods, obtain the best boon for us, your friends. O Soma, do thou flow toward our mission, the work of a messenger. Furthermore, since thou art poured out here for the sake of Indra, do thou ask the gods for the most excellent wealth on behalf of us, thy dear friends.

And we anoint you, the ruddy one, with products of the cow for exhilaration; open wide for us the doors to wealth. (3) And furthermore, O Soma, we—the descendants of Aṅgiras and Āyasya—anoint you, the ruddy-colored one, with products of the cow—that is, with milk—for the sake of exhilaration. "Kam" is a filler word. Therefore, you, for our wealth, open wide the doors. Open them for us.

The vigorous one has stepped across the filter, as a horse [steps] to the yoke on its path; Indu is master among the gods. Indu "is master" (*patyate*) and moves among the gods.

My friends have sung together for him who sports in the wood beyond the sheepskin; they have followed Indu with a ship. 5. "Mine," so [they cried]; my friends have sung together in the wood for him who sports beyond the sheepskin; they have followed Indu with a ship. 5.

They have been let loose for the feast of the gods, like swift steeds eager for victory, flowing forth, increasing upon the mountains. 1. They have been let loose for the feast of the gods; like swift steeds eager for victory, they flow, swelling upon the mountains. 1.

The Somas, which have grown on the mountains, increased by means of the mountain-pressings, or born upon the mountains, flow for the feast of the gods, for the sacrifice; like swift horses fit for action, they have been released and are being poured forth.

Like a well-adorned woman who honors her father, the drops of Soma have been poured forth for Vāyu. 2. The drops, like a well-adorned woman who honors her father, the Soma juices, have been released for Vāyu. 2.

The drops, the Soma juices being prepared at the sacrifices—well-adorned, beautifully decorated, and possessing the quality of the fathers (*pityāvatī*)—flow toward Vāyu, just as a well-adorned maiden belonging to the fathers goes toward her chosen bridegroom.

The drops (*indavas*), the Dāsas, rich in milk and rich in food—these Soma juices, being present in this rite, pressed out upon the two skin-pressing boards, being well-extracted and accompanied by ritual acts, strengthen Indra; that is to say, they cause him to flourish.

Run hither, O ye of skillful hands; seize the bright juices with the *manthin* vessel. Mix the exhilarating draught with milk. 4. Run hither! O ye of skillful hands! Seize the bright [juices]! With the *manthin*, mix the exhilarating [Soma] with milk! 4.

come toward me now!

Flow on, O Soma, winner of wealth, bestower of great riches, finding the path for us. 5. Flow on, O Soma, winner of wealth, bestower of great riches, finding the path for us. 5.

O Dhanañjaya, conqueror of people belonging to the enemy, O Soma, finder of the path (*gātuvit*), provider of the desired way, you who are the giver and bestower of great wealth (*mahaḥ rādhasaḥ*) upon us—such as you, flow and pour forth! The ten fingers cleanse this youth, the purifying one, for Indra—the exhilarating intoxication. (6) They cleanse him; they purify the youth, the flowing one, the ten fingers (the *kṣip* being a name for fingers, as found in the list of names). For the sake of Indra, they cleanse this exhilarating, intoxicating Soma in the filter. By this skillful act, O Soma, you have grown even toward the great ones. Rejoicing, you indeed swell. (1) By this beautiful performance, characterized by excellent praise and the like, Soma has grown toward even the great gods; he has increased. Rejoicing, taking delight, he "swells" (*udve pāyate*); that is, he acts like a bull. Just as a bull bellowing with joy makes a sound, so too at the time of pressing, he makes a sound in the sounding-holes (*uparava*). His deeds, his works, which crush the Dasyus, are perceived. And the bold one gathers the debts. (2) The deeds of this Soma, which are the destroyers of the Dasyus—that is, the Asuras—are recognized as such. And the bold Soma, through the granting of desires, gathers away even the debts of the sacrificers. Then the Soma, the sensory essence, becomes a thunderbolt, a subduer of force, when his hymn of praise (*uktha*) is born. (3) When the hymn of praise for this [Soma] comes into being, immediately thereafter the sensory essence, the powerful thunderbolt, the invincible Soma, becomes a subduer of force (*sahasasā*)—that is, a giver of immeasurable wealth to us. He himself, the seer (*kavi*), the distributor, seeks treasure for the sage when he thoroughly cleanses the prayers. (4) If this Soma, the seer whose actions are far-reaching, is thoroughly cleansed by the prayers—that is, by the fingers (there is a change of case; *dhiyaḥ* means by the *dhītis*, i.e., the fingers)—then he himself, for the wise distributor, for Indra the ordainer of desires, seeks the treasure, the delightful wealth. the meaning is that you conquer the enemies and bestow wealth upon them.

Flow forth for us, O Soma; pour down well upon us from heaven the rain of the waters, the wave of the waters. Flow forth health-giving, great refreshments, free from disease. Flow forth for us, O Soma; pour down well upon us from heaven the rain of the waters, the wave of the waters. Flow forth health-giving, great refreshments, free from disease. O Soma, flow forth for us from the world of heaven; pour down rain upon us. This very thing he shows: flow forth from heaven the wave of the waters. Moreover, flow forth health-giving, great refreshments—foods free from disease and free from affliction.

Flow with that stream by which the cattle of the enemy tribes have come here to our house. With that stream, flow; with that stream by which the cattle belonging to the enemy tribes have come here to our house. O Soma, flow with such a stream. Of what kind? He says: with such a stream as yours, the cattle belonging to the enemy tribes (*janya*) have come here to this world, into our house.

Flow with a stream of clarified butter, you who are most beloved by the gods in the sacrifices; flow toward us with rain. 3. Clarified butter! Flow with a stream in the sacrifices, O you who are most desired by the gods; for us, flow down rain. 3. O Soma, you who are most beloved by the gods (*devavītamaḥ*)—meaning you who intensely desire the gods—in the sacrifices, flow (*pavasva*) with a stream (*dhārayā*), that is, by means of your outpouring, as clarified butter (*ghṛtam*), which is water (since "clarified butter" is listed among the names for water); flow for us, the Bhrigus and the seers (*kavibhyaḥ*). And flow down (*ā pava*) rain (*vṛṣṭim*).

Flow through the sheep’s-wool filter with your stream for our nourishment; O Soma, you who are pressed, flow forth! For the gods indeed hear your call. O Soma, being pressed, flow through the sheep’s-wool filter with your stream for our strength (ūrja). O gods, they shall surely hear your sound produced at the time of your departure.

Flowing forth, he has sped away; he has struck down the demons. As of old, he causes the lights to shine. 5. Flowing forth, he has sped away; he has struck down the demons; as of old, causing the lights to shine. 5.

The twenty-seventh hymn, consisting of five verses, beginning with "adhvaryo," is the seerhood of Uvadhyā, the descendant of Aṅgiras. It is in the Gāyatrī meter and has Pavamāna Soma as its deity. Thus it is enumerated: "adhvaryo. The application of the hymn has been explained. 1. O Adhvaryu, release the pressed Soma through the filter with the stones; purify it for Indra to drink. 2. O Adhvaryus, press out for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the most honey-sweet Soma—the supreme nectar of heaven. 3. O Indu (Soma), these gods and the Maruts partake of that exhilarating food of yours, the flowing juice. 4. For you, O Soma, being pressed, increase [the gods] for the sake of swift exhilaration; O showerer of desires, come to the singer for his protection. 5. Flow toward the filter with your stream, O far-seeing one, being pressed; flow toward us for strength and fame. The twenty-eighth hymn, consisting of five verses, begins with "pari yukṣaḥ. The seers are Kaṇva and others, as before. It is enumerated: "pari yukṣaḥ. The application has been stated. 1. May the radiant one, winning wealth, bring us strength with his food; being pressed, flow into the filter. *Note: In verse 1, "sanadrayiḥ" means "winning wealth"; "andhasā" refers to the food or juice; "suvānaḥ" means "being pressed"; and "ā arpa" means "flow into. In verse 5, "vicakṣaṇa" means "far-seeing"; "dhārayā" means "with a stream"; and "uta śravaḥ" means "and fame."*

With your ancient, radiant paths, O beloved one, the thousand-streamed essence flows through the fleece of the sheep, extending far and wide. O Soma, your own essence—dear to the gods, bringing them delight, possessing a thousand streams, and vast in its strength—flows with its ancient, shining paths through the woolly filter of the sheep’s fleece, moving all around.

O Soma, call forth for us one who possesses wealth; O Indu, call forth now for the gift. O you whose nature is to strike with blows, call forth with your weapons! 3. *curaḥ* | *na* | *yaḥ* | *tam* | *īhaya* | *indo* | *na* | *dānam* | *īhaya* | *vadhaiḥ* | *vadhasno* | *īhaya* || 3 || O Soma, like a thief (*curaḥ*), call forth him who has abundant food (*pūrṇodanaḥ*); bring him to us. Furthermore, O Indu, now call forth the gift that is to be given. O *vadhasno*, O Soma whose color is brightened by striking, call forth [us] with your weapons—your blows upon the vital breaths!

O Indu, invoked by many, subdue the strength of those people who, being radiant, incite against us for the sake of harming us. [Subdue] that strength of these enemies; [subdue it], O radiant one—this is the sense.

O Indu, flow for us with a hundred aids, or indeed with a thousand of thy pure portions; flow as one who bestows abundant wealth. The hymn beginning with "utte" consists of four verses; it is the twenty-ninth hymn. It is the seerly work of Avatsāra Kāśyapa, composed in the Gāyatrī metre, dedicated to Pavamāna Soma. Thus it has been enumerated: "utte catuṣkam avatsāraḥ. The application (viniyoga) has already been stated.

And your bright streams have risen up, O wielder of the stone, cleaving asunder the demon; drive away those rival hosts that press around us! And your bright streams have risen up, O wielder of the stone, cleaving asunder the demon; drive away those rival hosts that press around us! O wielder of the stone, O Soma, your bright streams—your radiant, impetuous flows—have risen up, cleaving and rending asunder the demons (rākṣasas). Drive away those rival hosts—the contending enemy armies that obstruct us; that is to say, repel them.

With this power, by which you have subdued [the enemies] with force in the clash of chariots when the prize was staked—I shall praise you with a heart free from fear. 1. *ga*—expanded essence; *ta9*, *bha1.7*—expanded essence. 2. *ga*, *ta1.2.3.4*, *bha1.2*—full food; *ta6*, *bha7*—full-eating; *bha4*—full-eating. O Soma, you are one who, by this performed power (*ojasā*) and strength (*ayā*), possesses the habit of striking down enemies with force (*nijṛbhiḥ*). In the encounter of chariots (*rathasaṅge*) when the wealth (*dhane*) is at stake, I shall praise you with a heart that does not tremble (*arbibhyuṣā hṛdā*).
I, joined with a fearless heart and mind, praise you—that one—in the encounter of chariots, when our chariots meet, for the sake of the enemy being struck down and for the sake of wealth.
The inviolable vows of this one being purified cannot be assailed; shatter him who attacks you.
His vows cannot be assailed; O difficult-to-overcome one, shatter him who seeks to fight against you as you flow on. || 3 ||
O Soma Pavamāna, you whose sacred laws and deeds cannot be assailed by a malevolent-minded Rākṣasa, you who are invincible—crush and repel that evil-minded enemy who seeks to attack you in battle.
They urge him on— the exhilarating Indu, the tawny steed who distills intoxication— into the rivers for Indra.
They urge him on—the tawny, exhilarating one who distills intoxication, the spirited Indu, for Indra, into the rivers. 4.

The officiating priests urge forth—that is, they impel—for the sake of Indra, into the rivers (the *vasatīvarī* waters), that Soma, the drop (*indu*), which is the shaker of intoxication (*madacyuta*), the golden-hued (*hari*) one, the powerful (*vājin*), the exhilarating (*matsara*), and the most excellent.

From her, the ancient, bright, and radiant milk— the seer who wins a thousandfold— has been milked.
Following his ancient splendor, the days have milked out the bright, thousand-winning bull. 1.

Following this ancient, primordial, and radiant body of Soma—the brilliant one who bestows the thousandfold desired and immeasurable, the seer who beholds the fruit of transcendent actions—the wise sages milked, and continue to milk, the milk, that is, the essence to be drunk.
He is like the sun to behold; he rushes toward the lakes and the seven downward-flowing streams unto heaven.
This one, like the sun, is visible; he rushes toward the lakes, across the seven downward-flowing rivers, and up to heaven. 2.

This Soma is like the sun; just as the sun is the overseer of the entire world, so too is he the overseer (*upadṛk*) of ritual actions. Furthermore, this Soma [flows through] the lakes—some describe these as the thirty cups (*ukthapātra*).
Others, however, say that "sarāṃsi" refers to thirty days and nights;
he runs toward them, he goes toward them.

And thus Yāska says: "Regarding this, the ritualists inform us that there are thirty *uktha* cups at the midday pressing, dedicated to a single deity; they drink from these at that time with a single pouring. These are what are called 'sarāṃsi' here."
"Thirty days and nights belong to the dark fortnight and thirty to the bright fortnight," so say the etymologists (Nirukta 5.11).
Moreover, this Soma, with reference to heaven, stands upon seven precipices and seven rivers.
Being purified, this Soma stands above all worlds like the divine Sun.
This Soma, being purified, stands above all worlds like the divine Sun. 3.
Being purified and being cleansed, this Soma stands above all beings, above all worlds.
Regarding this, he provides an illustration:
like the divine Sun.
The meaning is that just as the divine sun stands above all worlds, so too does this Soma.

Flow around us with every nourishment, O Soma, and with all auspicious fortunes. (1) O Soma, flow around us with your stream—pour forth your juice again and again, repeatedly, through the *andhas* (the food-substance), so that there may be abundant nourishment for us. Furthermore, flow around us with all auspicious fortunes (*saubhagā*) and all riches. In this verse, the reduplication (*dvirbhāva*) of *puṣṭam-puṣṭam* occurs because the supplicant is extremely afflicted by thirst, according to Pāṇini’s rule *ābādhe ca* (8.1.10). It has been stated that affliction is a property of the speaker (*prayoktṛ-dharma*), not a property of the object denoted (*abhidheya-dharma*). Moreover, flow around us with all auspicious fortunes and all riches.

And furthermore, O Soma, finder of cattle and finder of horses, flow for us with your juice through these most rapid days. 3. He who conquers and does not decay, who slays the enemy fearlessly—he, O conqueror by force, flow for us. Approaching the enemy fearlessly—that is, approaching the enemy while remaining yourself free from fear—you slay him and are not yourself overcome by the enemies. As such, flow and purify yourself. Being purified, O lover of songs, O golden-hued Soma, being released toward the milk-mixture, create wide space and strength for the people. Being purified—O lover of songs, O golden-hued one, being released toward the milk-mixture, being cleansed, do thou create wealth and food for the person, that is, for the sacrificer.

Being purified for the feast of the gods, go to the appointed place of Indra—O Soma, shining with clarity, joined by the vigorous sacrificers, being cleansed for the sake of the sacrifice, proceed to the prepared abode of Indra. 15. Being purified... for the feast of the gods... of Indra... go... to the prepared place... shining with clarity... by the vigorous ones... joined. 15. O Soma, shining with clarity (*ghṛtānaḥ*), joined (*yataḥ*) by the vigorous (*vājibhiḥ*) sacrificers, being purified (*punānaḥ*) for the feast of the gods (*devavītaye*)—that is, for the sake of the sacrifice—go (*yāhi*) to the prepared place (*niṣkṛtam*) of Indra. 38.

Being urged forward, the swift drops of Soma, impelled by the prayer, have flowed forth toward the ocean. 16 The swift, vigorous drops of Soma, being urged forward and impelled by the prayer—that is, by the fingers—have been released toward the ocean, which is the intermediate space (antarikṣa). 16 *Note:* "Āśavaḥ" means possessing speed; "indavaḥ" refers to the Soma drops; "samudram" refers to the intermediate space; "accha" means toward; "hinvānāsaḥ" means being urged or impelled; "dhiyā" means by the prayer or by the fingers; "jūtāḥ" means driven or drawn forth; and "prāsuṣukṣata" means they are poured forth or released.

Being cleansed, the active drops, moving at will, have entered the ocean, the womb of cosmic order (ṛta). *Being cleansed*, *the active ones*—the goers; *the drops*, the Soma juices; *at will*, without effort; *into the ocean*, they go toward the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*). This very point he demonstrates: *they have gone to*, they enter, *the womb*, the place of origin, *of cosmic order*, that is, of water.

Go around us, desiring us, with all riches and with vigor; protect our hero-filled shelter. 18 O Soma, you who desire us (*asmayu*), go around (*pari yāhi*) us with all (*viśvā*) riches (*vasūni*) and with power (*ojasā*) for the sake of protection. Furthermore, protect (*pāhi*) our home (*śarma*) which is filled with heroes (*vīravat*), that is, with sons. 18
1. In Ga, Ta, Bha1, Bha2, and Bha7, the word "milk" (kṣīram) is not present.
2. In Ga, Ta, Bha1, Bha2, Bha4, and Bha5, it reads "for the sake of people" (janārtham).
3. In Ga, it reads "they are emitted" (prasṛjyante); in Ta and Bha2, it reads "it is emitted" (sṛjyate).
4. Arrival at ta1, ta2, ta3, ta4, ta5, ta6, bha1, bha2, and bha7; arrival at bha4.

The carrier, Etaśa, neighs as he yokes his station with hymns, when he is placed forward in the ocean. (19) He neighs—the carrier, Etaśa, yoking his station with *ṛc*s, when he is placed forward in the ocean. (19) O Soma, when that carrier, the horse Etaśa, neighs—that is, makes a sound—and while yoking his station in the sacrifice with the *ṛc*s, the officiating priests and chanters, and arriving for the sake of hearing the hymns, then you, the soul who carries the sacrifice, are placed forward in the ocean, that is, in the waters known as the *vasatīvarīs*.

When the swift one settles upon the golden womb of *ṛta*, he abandons those who lack wisdom. (20) When the swift, impetuous Soma settles upon the golden (*hiraṇyaya*) womb—the sacrificial place of *ṛta* (as it is said, "the gold-handed one presses [it]"), then at that moment he abandons and casts off those who are witless (*apracetasaḥ*). The meaning is that he does not approach the sacrifice of those who do not praise him, but rather approaches only the sacrifice of those who do praise him. (39)

The longing ones have sung in praise; the wise desire to sacrifice, while the senseless sink down. (21) The *venas*—the longing, beautiful singers—have sung aloud (*anūṣata*) in praise of Soma. The wise (*pracetasaḥ*), being well-disposed, desire to sacrifice (*iyakṣanti*). The "senseless" (*avicetasaḥ*)—meaning those whose minds are not distinguished, or rather, those whose minds are perverted—sink down (*majjanti*). The meaning is that those who do not praise Soma nor perform sacrifice fall into hell.

Flow, O Indu, most rich in sweetness, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, to sit upon the seat of Ṛta. Flow, O Indu, most rich in sweetness, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, to sit upon the seat of Ṛta. O Indu, Soma, most rich in sweetness—exceedingly full of honey—to sit upon the seat, the place of Ṛta, the sacrifice; flow, purify yourself, for the sake of Indra who is accompanied by the Maruts. Flow, pour forth.

The wise sages, skilled in speech and performers of rites, adorn you; the living men cleanse you thoroughly. (23) O Soma, those wise ones—learned in sacred speech and performers of rituals—adorn you, the purifying one. Furthermore, the living men cleanse you perfectly. (23)

O Sage Soma, Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa, and the Maruts—all these gods drink your juice as you flow forth, O Pavamāna. 24. Your juice, O Sage, Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa, and the Maruts drink as you, the Pavamāna, flow forth. O Sage, O Soma of lovely deeds, as you flow, all these gods—Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa, and the Maruts—drink your juice.

O Soma, being purified, you send forth inspired speech, O Indu, which brings a thousandfold bounty. 25. You, O Soma, being purified, send forth inspired speech, O Indu, which brings a thousandfold bounty. 25.
1. *ga*-yadīyo; 2. *ga*-yadā ṛgbhiḥ; 3. *ta*1.2.6.7-*mu*-padaṃ yujāno yajñe yujāno; *ta*5-*padaṃ yajñe yujānau yujāno*; 4. *ta*3-*bha*1.7-*bhavati*; 5. *ga*-dhāvitaro (? vidhātāro).

O brilliant Indu, Soma, being purified and cleansed, you impel the threefold wisdom, the filter, and the speech that brings a thousandfold support—that is, speech which provides much sustenance. || 40 || And furthermore, O Soma, O Indu, being purified, bring to us the speech that brings a thousandfold support and that yearns for the sacrifice. || 26 || And furthermore, O Soma, O Indu, being purified, bring to us the speech that brings a thousandfold support and that yearns for the sacrifice. || 26 || And moreover, O brilliant Indu, Soma, being purified and cleansed, bring to us the speech that brings a thousandfold support, that yearns for wealth, and that desires the sacrifice; bring it here!
