‘Vārita’—the particle ‘id’ is used here for emphasis. [He] desires only water; likewise, I desire your protection (*parilavaṇa*). Therefore: “O Indu, flow around for Indra. || 25 || The tenth hymn, consisting of eleven verses beginning with ‘Śaryaṇāvati’, is the seerly composition (*ārṣam*) of Kaśyapa, the son of Marīci. Since the word ‘hi’ was mentioned previously, this and the following [hymns] are in the Paṅkti meter. They have Pavamāna Soma as their deity. Thus it is enumerated: “In ‘Śaryaṇāvati’, eleven [verses]; Kaśyapa [is the seer]. The application (*viniyoga*) has been explained. May Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, drink the Soma at Śaryaṇāvat; placing strength within himself, performing great heroic deeds—O Indu, flow around for Indra! || 1 || At Śaryaṇāvat: may Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, drink the Soma. Of what nature? Placing strength within himself, depositing strength therein, and thus performing great heroic deeds against his enemies. Therefore, O Indu, flow around for Indra! Flow hither, O Lord of the Quarters, from Ārjīka, O bountiful Soma! Pressed by means of the word of Truth, by truth, by faith, and by austerity—O Indu, flow around for Indra! || 2 || O Lord of the Quarters—the quarters being the East and so forth—you who illuminate them; O bountiful Soma, from Ārjīka: the region of Ārjīka is that which is not far from the Ṛjīkas. From there, flow hither toward our sacrifice. Or rather: flow from the straight, non-crooked, purifying [filter]. Of what nature? Pressed by those initiated ones endowed with the word of Truth, with truth, with faith, and with austerity—flow! The daughter of the Sun brought that bull, grown by Parjanya; the Gandharvas received him. They placed that essence in Soma—O Indu, flow around for Indra! || 3 || Grown by Parjanya: capable like Parjanya. Or rather, grown by water, which is the effect of Parjanya. That bull—great or worshipful—Soma, she brought; she fetched it from the heavenly world. The Gandharvas, Viśvāvasu and others, received him; they took hold of him. With joy and vigor, the Gandharvas then placed that received essence into Soma. [This is from the root] *dhā* in the *laṅ* tense. Therefore, flow around! || 3 ||
1. *vāri* (water) occurs in Ta 4.5.7; *vāḥ* (waters) occurs in Ta 3.6 and Bha 1.2.4.7; *vārida* (giver of water) occurs in Bha 6.
2. In the sense of "holding" (*dhāraṇe*), *tara* occurs in Bha 6.
O Pavamāna, in that world where all light—that is, every splendor—exists eternally and imperishably.
And in this world, wherein the light called Āditya is placed and established,
in that world which is immortal— free from the nature of death— and therefore undecaying, place me, who am performing the pressing of Soma; therefore,
flow forth for Indra in order to lead me to the highest world.

Where King Vaivasvata dwells, where the enclosure of heaven is, where those great waters flow—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra. (8) Where King Vaivasvata is, where the enclosure of heaven is, where those great waters are—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra. (8)
In that world where Vivasvat’s son, Yama, is the king;
and in that world where the hiding place of the sun, Diva, is the entrance for all beings;
moreover, in that world where these great waters, such as the Gaṅgā and others, abide.
In that world, O such one, make me immortal—devoid of the nature of death;
that is to say, lead me to the state of divinity.
Therefore, flow forth.

Where there is movement at will in the triple-heavened third sky of the heavens, where the worlds are full of light—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra! 9. Where there is movement according to desire in the triple-heavened third sky of the heavens, where the worlds are luminous—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra! 9.
There, in the third heaven, in the third celestial world, in the triple firmament—

where there are three abodes existing by way of lower, middle, and upper levels— in that third firmament, in the highest place, there is the movement of *div*, the Sun, according to his desires (*anukāmam*).
Moreover, in that world where the worlds are luminous, endowed with light—
make me immortal in such a world;
so that my highest world may come to be, flow forth for Indra.

Where desires and fulfilled wishes abide, where the realm of the sun is found, where there is self-sustenance and satisfaction—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow forth for Indra! 10. Where desires and fulfilled wishes abide, where the realm of the sun is found, where there is self-sustenance and satisfaction—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow forth for Indra! 10.
In this world where the *kāmāḥ*—the gods who are desired—and the *nikāmāḥ*—Indra and others who are most certainly and necessarily prayed for—are present;
or alternatively, where the *kāmāḥ*, *nikāmāḥ*, and *abhilāṣāḥ* (desires and longings) exist;
in this world of *bradhna*, the illuminator of all.
Or rather:

since rituals do not come to pass without the Sun, in that world where the *viṣṭapa*—the dwelling place—of Āditya, who is the root of all rituals, exists; in that world where *svadhā*—food, or food given with the utterance *svadhā*, or satisfaction, or satiation, or joy—is found; in that world, make me immortal.
1. Perform [it] in four ways. 2.
You [are so] because of the cause consisting of the three gates and the five factors.
3. It does not engage in action.

Where blisses and joys, delights and raptures abide, where the desires of desire are attained—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra. (11) *Yatra* (where), *ānandāḥ* (blisses), *ca* (and), *modāḥ* (joys), *ca* (and), *mudaḥ* (delights), *pramudaḥ* (raptures), *āsate* (abide); *kāmasya* (of desire), *yatra* (where), *āptāḥ* (attained), *kāmāḥ* (desires); *tatra* (there), *mām* (me), *amṛtam* (immortal), *kṛdhi* (make); *indrāya* (for Indra), *indo* (O Indu), *pari* (around), *srava* (flow). (11) In whichever world blisses and the others abide—their specific distinctions should be observed—and in whichever world all the desires of desire, that is, of the desired deity, are attained and reached, there make me immortal. "This cannot happen without you"; therefore, O Soma, flow around. (27) The eleventh hymn, consisting of four verses beginning with "ya indoḥ," has its seer and other details as before. Thus it is enumerated: "ya indoścatuṣkam" (the four-verse hymn beginning with ya indoḥ). The application of the hymn has been explained.

He who has followed the stations of the flowing Indu, him they call "one of noble progeny," O Soma, he who has won over your mind for Indra; flow around, O Indu! He who has followed the stations—meaning the places such as the *droṇakalaśa* vessel, or alternatively, the splendors—of the flowing Indu, the Soma; that Brāhmaṇa who follows them, him people call "one of noble progeny" (*suprajāḥ*), meaning one possessed of excellent offspring, such as virtuous sons and so forth. (The suffix *-as* is added by the rule *nityamasica prajā-maitrayoḥ*). The sense is: he who presses the Soma becomes endowed with sons and other blessings. Furthermore, O Soma, he who fixes his mind upon you—that is, who wins over your mind or attends to you—the root *vidhati* here meaning "to attend"—him too they call one of noble progeny. Therefore, flow around for us.

O Seer, with the hymns of the composers of mantras, Kaśyapa has magnified his songs; pay homage to Soma, the King, who was born as the Lord of plants. O Indu, flow forth for Indra! (2) The Seer addresses himself: "O Seer, O Kaśyapa, you who perceive the hymns—by means of the praises (*stomaiḥ*) of the seers who compose the mantras, you have caused these songs (*giraḥ*), which are in the form of eulogies, to increase higher and higher. Pay homage—that is, worship—the King, the sovereign of all, that Soma. [The suffix *kyac* is applied to the root *namas* in the sense of 'worship,' according to Pāṇini 3.1.19]. Worship him, that Soma who was born as the Lord and protector of the various plants and trees. O Indu, flow forth so that you may be pressed by yourself."
1. *ta-bhara-prajanaḥ* | 2. They say it is *tara-bhaya-janam*; *bha1.2* say it is *janayin*; *bha6* says the meaning is *janam*. 3.
*ta1.2.5.6.7-bha6-mu* say "worship with *manasā*"; *bha7* says "worship with *namasā*".

The seven directions have various suns; there are seven hotṛ-priests, the officiating ministers; there are the seven divine Ādityas—with them, O Soma, protect us. For Indra, O Indu, flow around! 3. Seven directions; having various suns; seven; hotṛ-priests; officiating ministers; gods; the Ādityas; who; seven; with them; O Soma; protect; us; for Indra; O Indu; flow around. 3.
There are seven directions.
Excluding the direction in which the Moon resides, there are seven others.
There are seasons presided over by various suns; that is, they are governed by different kinds of solar orbs.
This is because of the scriptural tradition: "The various sacrificial fires have various suns" (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 1.7).
Alternatively, "having various suns" is an epithet qualifying the directions.
Likewise, there are seven officiating priests (*ṛtvij*), beginning with the *hotṛ* and others, who perform the *vaṣaṭ*-utterance.
Furthermore, there are the seven gods who are the sons of Aditi (*ādityas*)—Dhātṛ and the rest—excluding Mārtāṇḍa.
This point will be elaborated upon in the verse: "Eight sons are there of Aditi" (*Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 10.72.8).
O Soma, protect us with all those [elements], such as the quarters and so forth;
for without you, this cannot be accomplished. Therefore, O Indu, flow forth for Indra.

In the *upākaraṇa* and *utsarjana* rites, during the oblation within the maṇḍala, the verse is “*yatte rājan*. This is also stated in the Sūtra: “‘*yatte rājañchṛtaṃ haviḥ*’ and ‘*samānī va ākṛtiḥ*’ is one [verse]” (Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra 3.5.7–8).

O King Soma, with that oblation which has been prepared for you, protect us on every side. Let not the enemy overcome us, and let nothing whatsoever afflict us. Flow around for Indra, O Indu! That which is yours, O King, the heard oblation—with that, O Soma, protect us. Let not the hostile one overcome us, and let nothing whatsoever cause us pain. Flow around for Indra, O Indu!

O King, O Lord Soma, whatever oblation (*havis*) has been cooked (*śr̥tam*) for you— *śr̥tam* being derived from the root *śr̥* in the sense of cooking according to Pāṇini’s rule 6.1.27— as a means for accomplishing all our rites,
protect us with that oblation.
Protect us!
Therefore, let no enemy—one possessing enmity—overcome or slay us, who are protected by you.
Furthermore, let the enemy not harm (*āmamat*) even the slightest thing of ours, such as wealth and the like.
Whatever has been stated by these hymns, [it means]: "O Indu, flow forth for Indra in such a way that it becomes ours.

Thus, by means of these hymns beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā" and ending with this [verse], the manifold Soma to be brought forth has been extolled; therefore, it is implied that the Soma sacrifice must be performed for the sake of attaining fruits both in this world and the next.
Thus ends the seventh Anuvāka in the ninth Maṇḍala of the Dāśatayī, in the Mādhavīya Vedārthaprakāśa composed by Sāyaṇācārya; and the ninth Maṇḍala is completed.
1. "O King, [it is] thus. 2. "It has been heard, it has been heard," [said] Ta, Ta, Cha, Pa, Ya, Sa, and Ma.
